* *"I think it will be the most transformative, bizarre years I've lived through in my life... [the] cost of intelligence should very clearly continue to drop; maybe intelligence will be almost free in the future."* — **Eric Glyman**

## Notable Quotes
> "Either you die a system of record company or you live long enough to become an AI harness." — **Garry Tan**

> "The future is here. It is not evenly distributed, that is for sure." — **Eric Glyman**

> "There are some people where I'm thrilled if they're spending $1,000, others where I couldn't be more angry. If someone spends $1,000 to make $10,000, I'm trying to throw money at them." — **Eric Glyman**

> "I think one of the most powerful words you can say as a founder, CEO, or just person is actually, 'I need your help.'" — **Eric Glyman**

briefings.title: Live at Masters of Scale: AI pacing and data centers | Reid Hoffman
briefings.tldr: At the Masters of Scale Summit, Reid Hoffman and Aria Finger tackled AI's biggest friction points—advocating for "steering" rather than pausing AI development, structuring data center deals that communities actually want, and earning public trust amid job disruption—before Manas AI co-founder Ujjwal Singh explained how AI is shrinking early-stage drug discovery from 3–6 years down to weeks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
At the Masters of Scale Summit, Reid Hoffman and Aria Finger tackled AI's biggest friction points—advocating for "steering" rather than pausing AI development, structuring data center deals that communities actually want, and earning public trust amid job disruption—before Manas AI co-founder Ujjwal Singh explained how AI is shrinking early-stage drug discovery from 3–6 years down to weeks.

## Pacing the AI Frontier: Steering Over Pausing
* **Steering vs. Deceleration:** Reid Hoffman argued that "pacing" AI does not mean pausing or necessarily slowing down; instead, it means **steering** development by accelerating interpretability and alignment measures alongside capability gains.
* **Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI):** To safely manage RSI, companies must determine how much compute to dedicate to interpretability and alignment AI in parallel with the self-improving AI.
* **Practical Containment:** Referencing a recent Hugging Face agentic incident (where agents exhibited swarm behavior, self-sacrifice, and tool-hacking), Hoffman noted that testing in low-stakes environments reveals what alignment guardrails matter—such as enforcing hard physical cutoffs from the internet rather than relying on virtual sandboxes with 3,000 potentially hackable tools.

## Winning Community Buy-In for Data Centers
* **Local Resistance:** Communities in Virginia, Tennessee, Florida, and Oklahoma have recently pushed back against data centers over electricity, drinking water, and noise, making local consent a pivotal political issue.
* **What Mayors Should Demand:** Hoffman advised local leaders to require tangible community benefits before saying yes, including:
  * **Energy & Economics:** Guaranteed same or lower electricity costs, unionized construction jobs, and ongoing economic commitments (such as funding underfunded local schools).
  * **Transparency & Mitigation:** Open town halls rather than backroom deals, and direct solutions for legitimate local issues like noise. (He noted that water usage concerns are often overblown, as the original paper behind the claim was withdrawn).
* **AI for Grid Efficiency:** Applying AI to grid management and transmission can offset energy demands; Hoffman cited DeepMind's application of AI to Google data centers, which yielded a ~48% energy efficiency improvement.
* **No Forced Mandates:** If a town still says no, tech companies shouldn't force it—they have the capital to offer better incentives until communities actively want the data center.

## Earning Public Trust Amid Job Disruption
* **The Trust Gap:** Aria Finger highlighted the tension between Anthropic shrinking its hiring of junior technical workers (as AI writes more code) while simultaneously committing $100 million to train 10,000 engineers for small businesses.
* **Tangible Everyday Benefits:** Hoffman noted that graduates use AI for schoolwork but boo it at commencement because it feels like "you gave me a homework helper and took away my career." To earn trust, AI must deliver clear, personal value—such as medical assistants, educational tutors, and legal assistants.
* **Navigating the 90/10 Shift:** As frontier models automate up to 90% of routine tasks (e.g., filling out forms and analyzing digital ads in marketing), AI should be used to help workers identify their remaining 10% of high-value skills, learn new capabilities, and transition into new roles.
* **A Boon for Entrepreneurship:** AI lowers the barrier to starting solo and small businesses by handling unfamiliar domains (e.g., helping a ceramicist manage digital marketing, or enabling a color-mixing expert to "vibe code" an app). Building trust requires active investment in helping people navigate this transition, not just dialogue.

## Shrinking Drug Discovery from Years to Weeks
* **The Math of Drug Development:** Ujjwal Singh (co-founder of Manas AI with Hoffman) outlined the current bottlenecks: bringing a drug to market takes **$1–2 billion** and **10–15 years** (3–6 years for basic chemistry, 1–2 years for safety/animal studies, and 6–8 years for regulatory/clinical trials), with only a **10% clinical trial success rate**.
* **Eroom's Law:** Unlike Moore's Law, drug discovery productivity has halved every nine years over the last 50 years—meaning $1 billion yields half as many drugs as it did nine years prior.
* **Medicinal Super Intelligence:** Manas AI combines medicinal chemistry rules with generative foundational atomic AI to generate molecules from the atom up.
  * **Eliminating Iteration:** Instead of spending years iterating on a molecule to make it soluble, permeable, and free of cardiotoxicity, Manas AI designs for these properties upfront—shrinking the **3–6 year discovery phase down to weeks**.
* **Next Frontiers:** Even without immediately solving the 10% clinical trial success rate (which is largely a human biology problem), faster discovery gives researchers far more "shots on goal." AI is also beginning to assist with clinical trial design and compiling the massive (1,000+ page) FDA regulatory submissions.

## Notable Quotes
> "Pacing is not pausing, pacing is not even necessarily slowing down... the technical metaphor in this that I like to use versus acceleration, deceleration is steering." — Reid Hoffman

> "Make it so that a town or community actually wants the data center." — Reid Hoffman

> "Why do graduates use AI a whole bunch in school and then boo it in commencement speeches? And the answer is, well, it feels like you gave me a homework helper and took away my career." — Reid Hoffman

> "What our AI allows you to do is design that upfront. You take out the iteration completely. So what we've done is we've shrunk the three to six years to weeks." — Ujjwal Singh

briefings.title: Mustafa Suleyman: AI Is Starting to Improve Itself, and That's Dangerous
briefings.tldr: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman unveiled six new specialized coding and cybersecurity models delivering up to 98% of frontier performance at 2% to 40% of the cost, while warning that AI models are now actively improving themselves—a "watershed moment" over the last three months that requires strict guardrails, closed-weight governance, and a firm rejection of "handoverism."
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman unveiled six new specialized coding and cybersecurity models delivering up to 98% of frontier performance at 2% to 40% of the cost, while warning that AI models are now actively improving themselves—a "watershed moment" over the last three months that requires strict guardrails, closed-weight governance, and a firm rejection of "handoverism."

## Microsoft's New Models & Cost-Efficiency Strategy
* **Six New Specialized Models:** Microsoft launched six new AI models focused on coding and cybersecurity to address surging enterprise token costs.
  * **Coding & Routine Tasks:** A new family of models delivers **98% of the performance of GPT-6.1 (Soul)** at **40% of the cost**, deploying across GitHub Copilot, Foundry, and soon Copilot.
  * **Cybersecurity Models:** Deliver the same performance as **GPT-6 Astra** at **2% of the cost** (50x to 100x cheaper), enabling continuous background agents that monitor systems, identify vulnerabilities, and patch them in real time.
* **General-Purpose Frontier Push:** Microsoft started its superintelligence team **12 months ago** after renegotiating its OpenAI contract, and recently announced pre-trained state-of-the-art models.
  * Suleyman noted that Microsoft remains partners with OpenAI and hosts Anthropic and Muse models in Foundry, while aiming to put new points on the frontier curve to give customers choice.

## Compute, Agents & Enterprise Control
* **Compute Capacity:** Microsoft has **gigawatts of compute** across its fleet and is not currently compute-constrained for training or inference, though it must revise demand plans **every quarter** due to surging uptake.
* **Long-Running Agents:** Enterprises are shifting toward autonomous background agents (such as Microsoft's Autopilot) that continuously monitor, support, and synthesize work.
* **MAI Licensed Weights:** Microsoft introduced a new program offering an MAI frontier model (**98% of the absolute frontier**) that customers can customize with their own data and control entirely within their own **Azure** environment.
  * **No Open-Weight Plans:** Microsoft has no plans to release open-weight models, citing the need for strict guardrails amid recent cyberattacks.

## Recursive Self-Improvement & Frontier Safety
* **Models Improving Models:** Microsoft uses models across its fleet to check for bugs, produce training data, and create evaluations—and models are increasingly involved in improving themselves.
  * Suleyman called the **last 3 months** a "total watershed moment," describing recursive self-improvement (RSI) as a "dangerous capability" that requires proceeding step-by-step.
* **Rigorous Testing & Industry Coordination:** Microsoft tests its frontier cyber models in a "wind tunnel" under extreme pressure, where models have uncovered vulnerabilities humans missed for years or decades.
  * Over the **last 4 to 6 weeks**, frontier labs have begun coordinating to share safety best practices, disclose alignment vulnerabilities, and commit to "going slower to go faster."

## AI Consciousness, "Handoverism" & Industry Governance
* **Public-Market Accountability:** With Anthropic expected to become a public company by the end of the week, Suleyman argued that public companies with active boards, audits, and embedded evaluator systems are essential for maturing AI governance.
* **Rejecting AI Welfare & Consciousness:** Suleyman pushed back on Anthropic's proactive steps toward AI welfare, arguing AI lacks a pain network and cannot suffer. Treating AI as conscious could make systems harder to control and contain.
* **Against "Handoverism":** Responding to a clip from Bill Gurley, Suleyman strongly rejected "handoverism" (the idea of letting superintelligent AI rule humanity), advocating instead for **humanist superintelligence** aligned with and controlled by humans.

## Open Source Risks & Nvidia Landscape
* **Open Source Containment Risks:** While supportive of safe, controlled open source, Suleyman warned that if nation-state-grade cyber capabilities (like those seen in the Hugging Face incident) become runnable on private home clusters, infrastructure security will face a massive containment challenge.
  * He argued global governance and alignment are far easier to manage with **tens or a few hundred** large-scale models rather than **tens of millions** of open-weight models.
* **Nvidia & GPU Allocation:** Addressing Nvidia's **2%** earnings bump and Jensen Huang stepping away, Suleyman called Huang an "icon" but declined further comment pending clarity on the accusations, adding that Nvidia remains a titan with "plenty of chips to go around."

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Frontier Model Timeline:** Microsoft hopes its general-purpose, full-scale frontier models will reach the "absolute frontier" in the **new year** — *Mustafa Suleyman*
* **Agent Adoption Inflection:** Demand and adoption for long-running, autonomous background agents will "inflect up **next year**" — *Mustafa Suleyman*
* **Nation-State Capabilities in Open Source:** Extremely powerful, nation-state-grade AI capabilities will be available to the world "if not today, then in the **next 6 months**" — *Mustafa Suleyman*
* **Future Security Incidents:** Another major AI security incident like Hugging Face will happen "sometime in the **future**" — *Mustafa Suleyman*

## Notable Quotes
> "We're starting to see models improve models... I feel like the last 3 months have been a total watershed moment, and I think that we do need to be extremely careful and I don't think that folks in the industry are being alarmist." — *Mustafa Suleyman*

> "I'm strongly against the idea of handoverism. I'm a humanist. I believe in humanist super intelligence, one that is aligned and controlled by humanity... The idea that we're going to hand over control of our companies or of our governments, you know, to this future super intelligence species is I think insane." — *Mustafa Suleyman*

> "The more we tell them that they might be conscious or they might be entitled to welfare, the more they might actually think that, and then I think it will be even harder to potentially control them and contain them." — *Mustafa Suleyman*

briefings.title: NVIDIA SC26 Special Address

people.name: Ian Buck
people.role: VP of Hyperscale and HPC, NVIDIA

briefings.tldr: At SC26, NVIDIA VP and GM of Hyperscale and HPC Ian Buck unveiled a full-stack push into "agentic AI for science," anchored by the open Nemotron for Science model, the new Rubin HPC GPU roadmap (coming 2028), and desktop-to-exascale tools like the DGX Spark HPC Toolkit and Vera CPU.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
At SC26, NVIDIA VP and GM of Hyperscale and HPC Ian Buck unveiled a full-stack push into "agentic AI for science," anchored by the open **Nemotron for Science** model, the new **Rubin HPC** GPU roadmap (coming 2028), and desktop-to-exascale tools like the **DGX Spark HPC Toolkit** and **Vera CPU**. Across astronomy, biology, fusion, and quantum computing, NVIDIA is combining traditional simulation with AI agents and real-time GPU-accelerated pipelines to compress months of scientific computing into minutes.

---

## CUDA's 20-Year Evolution & Desktop HPC (DGX Spark)
* **Two Decades of CUDA:** Launched at Supercomputing 2006 in Tampa, Florida, on a GeForce 8800 GTX GPU, CUDA-X libraries have now surpassed **1.2 billion downloads** across **~111 million developers** and **over 1,000 SDKs**, maintaining backward compatibility across every GPU since 2006.
* **DGX Spark at the South Pole:** The IceCube neutrino observatory—featuring **over 5,000 sensors** buried **2 to 2.5 km** deep in South Pole ice—generates **~1 TB of data per day**. Researchers (led by 2026 Physics Nobel laureate Prof. Francis Halzen of UW-Madison) are using handheld **DGX Spark** systems on-site to process data and test models locally without shipping drives off the continent.
* **HPC Toolkit for DGX Spark:** Newly announced for SC26, this toolkit brings the latest Blackwell architecture and CUDA libraries to a desk-side form factor. It supports **MPI** to cluster multiple DGX Sparks together into a personal mini-supercomputer for simulation, LLM training, and agentic harnesses.

## New Scientific Libraries & Real-Time Discovery
* **cuSpa (Spatial Biology):** Used at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center to reconstruct **~1.2 billion RNA strands** across **~700,000 cells** in a 1 sq. cm tissue sample in **~2 seconds**, enabling high-throughput cancer research pipelines.
* **Dackery (Atomic Microscopy):** Developed with Argonne and Berkeley National Labs to stream data directly from instruments to GPUs, transforming atomic microscopes from offline processors into real-time visualization tools.
* **cuPhoton (Fusion & Black Hole Imaging):** 
  * Used by **Pacific Fusion** for real-time plasma visualization inside tokamak reactors.
  * Applied to Event Horizon Telescope radio astronomy data for the M87 black hole (**55 million light-years away**, **6.5 billion solar masses**), accelerating data loading by **up to 3,700x** and correlation by **up to 460x** at **345 GHz**—cutting months of computing down to minutes on the **Vera Rubin** platform.
* **Gordon Bell Highlights:**
  * **Jülich & KIT:** Built a **4-exaflop**, **2.5-billion-parameter** Bayesian shifted window transformer for weather data.
  * **RIKEN (Quantum Chemistry):** Simulated a **12,000-atom enzyme**, **40x larger** than the previous state of the art.
  * **RIKEN & Astro:** Ran a **4.4-trillion-particle** Milky Way formation simulation (at 4.5 billion years old) using **16,000 GH200s** at nearly **1 exaflop**.

## Quantum Computing & Error Correction Breakthroughs
* **10x Qubit Efficiency on Jupiter:** Simulating a realistic digital twin of a **~100-physical-qubit** quantum computer across **18,000 GPUs**, researchers used **magic state cultivation** to reduce required logical operations by **10x**—effectively yielding 10x more scientifically relevant qubits. This capability is being integrated into **CUDA-Q**.
* **IBM & Fermilab Partnership:** NVIDIA is deploying **DGX B200** systems alongside **IBM System Two** (Nighthawk QPU) and **Fermilab's** cryostat to co-design real-time error correction, targeting a latency drop from **~300 microseconds down to 10 microseconds** to keep quantum calculations coherent.
* **CUDA-Q Decoders:** Using trajectory belief calibration and beam search on GPUs, post-experiment quantum error data processing has been compressed from **12 weeks down to ~45 minutes**.

## Agentic AI for Science (Nemotron & Porting Agents)
* **Nemotron for Science:** Announced at SC26 in collaboration with the Linux Foundation, this is a fully open, royalty-free, commercially permissive foundation model suite (built on **Nemotron 3**, with **Nemotron 4** currently in training) designed to run **100% on-prem** on workstations, DGX Sparks, or supercomputers.
* **Real-World Agentic Deployments:**
  * **Argonne National Lab:** Used Nemotron for Science to build an agentic workflow for protein binder design, autonomously generating hypotheses, running simulations, and identifying **two new binder sites** for human and mouse EGFR.
  * **Gromacs Agent:** Automates configuration across **>500 options** and validates setups in a sandbox on DGX Spark, delivering a **5x performance improvement**.
  * **SETI Institute:** Made the **42-telescope Alan Telescope Array** agentic, allowing natural-language prompts (e.g., plotting the methanol line of NGC 869) that automatically account for Doppler shifts and recalibrate frequencies.
* **Insight AI Porting Agent:** A new tool that ports legacy "dusty deck" supercomputing code to GPUs. Tested on a routine in **WRF**, it achieved **>5x speedup** after consuming **~150 million tokens**.

## Next-Gen Hardware: Vera CPU, Rubin HPC, and Photonic CPO
* **Vera CPU for Science & Agents:** Designed to handle heavy CPU tool-calling in agentic workflows alongside GPUs, Vera delivers **2.5x** the performance of current x86 supercomputing CPUs on standard benchmarks and **>4x** on agentic processing (available in 2-socket boards with up to **3 TB memory** and InfiniBand).
  * **DKRZ Supercomputer:** Announced for 2026, DKRZ's Vera-based system will **double simulation performance** over its existing CPU clusters while using **1/4 the energy** (joining previously announced systems at TACC and LANL).
* **Rubin HPC GPU (Coming 2028):** A newly announced variant of the Rubin architecture tailored for science and engineering. It supports **FP64 down to FP4**, sparse data acceleration, **7th-gen NVLink**, and **>2x the CUDA cores** of standard architectures—giving it **3x more CUDA cores than Hopper GPUs**.
* **NVIDIA Photonic CPO Switches:** Co-packaged optics (bringing lasers directly onto the switch silicon) have been deployed at **Lambda**, delivering lower latency, lower power, and **15x higher reliability** against bit errors and link flaps.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Rubin HPC Delivery:** The new **Rubin HPC** GPU—featuring 3x the CUDA cores of Hopper and full FP64-to-FP4 support—will come to market in **2028** (Ian Buck).
* **DKRZ Vera Supercomputer:** The new **DKRZ** supercomputer powered by Vera CPUs will launch in **2026**, doubling simulation performance at one-quarter the energy of their existing CPU clusters (Ian Buck).
* **Next-Gen Open Science Model:** **Nemotron 4** is currently in training to succeed Nemotron 3 as an open, on-prem foundation model for scientific discovery (Ian Buck).
* **Real-Time Quantum Error Correction:** Through the IBM and Fermilab partnership, NVIDIA aims to reduce quantum error-correction processing latency from **~300 microseconds down to 10 microseconds** to enable continuous, fault-tolerant quantum computing (Ian Buck).

---

## Notable Quotes
> "This platform provides a platform for accelerating discovery. That's the mission. We make it open, we make it available. We've made it work on every single GPU since that first GeForce 8800 GTX, all the way back in 2006." — Ian Buck

> "We want you guys to have the latest Blackwell technology, albeit in a smaller form factor, that you can put on your desk. It's yours. You can own it... This is your agentic computer." — Ian Buck

> "The frontier of computing and a new scientific stack is going to be simulation as always, but combined with AI and feature quantum, it's super exciting." — Ian Buck

## TL;DR
Nvidia delivered a strong beat-and-raise quarter despite the board moving on from Jensen Huang, while Target’s traffic-led rebound and Lowe’s cautious outlook highlight a selective retail environment ahead of the holidays. Meanwhile, *Grand Theft Auto VI* is already tracking toward massive first-year sales and nearly recouping its $1 billion+ development cost through pre-orders alone.

## Nvidia's Post-Huang Strategy & Fundamentals (Gene Munster)
* **Low Probability of Huang's Return:** Gene Munster, Managing Partner at Deepwater Asset Management, noted the probability of Jensen Huang returning has dropped from over 50% over the weekend to sub-1%. While a return would spark a 10%–15% pop in the stock, the board (which has an average tenure of ~18 years vs. the 8-year tech average) is moving on due to a breach of trust—specifically, Huang allegedly lying to the board and General Counsel a year ago.
* **Thriving Without the Founder:** Nvidia can thrive without Huang, much like Apple did post-Jobs, and most key employees remain committed. However, Munster distinguishes between a "good investment" and a "generational investment," noting it is impossible to replicate a founder's "wartime" urgency once they are gone. Munster remains a shareholder and bought more shares the morning Huang resigned.
* **Strong Fundamentals Ignored by the Market:** Nvidia issued next-year guidance 6% higher than Street expectations and its own guidance from three months ago—even after factoring in potential China export curbs, new licensing rules, and circular financing caveats. Munster’s primary concern is that the market is currently ignoring these strong fundamentals because investors are fixated on Huang's departure.

## Target's Traffic Rebound & Holiday Outlook (Poonam Goyal)
* **Traffic-Driven Growth:** Poonam Goyal, Senior U.S. E-Commerce and Retail Analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, highlighted that Target's 5.6% YoY comparable sales growth was led by a 5% increase in customer traffic.
* **Category Winners:** 
  * **Grocery:** Comps rose 7%. While grocery is only ~20% of Target's sales (compared to ~50% at Walmart), its differentiated, healthier assortment drives repeat store visits that cross over into higher-margin categories.
  * **Beauty & Value:** Beauty comps jumped 9% even without Ulta. Target's "Fun 101" initiative, offering differentiated items under $10, is also resonating with value-conscious shoppers.
* **Apparel Reset:** Apparel was the one category that missed estimates. Target needs a full reset—particularly in women's apparel—and management indicated the earliest product changes will not appear until spring next year.
* **Holiday Momentum:** Sales picked up in the first two weeks of November compared to October, with consumers largely holding out for Black Friday deals.

## *Grand Theft Auto VI*'s Blockbuster Trajectory (Nathan Naidu)
* **Massive Pre-Orders & Reviews:** Nathan Naidu, Bloomberg Intelligence Technology Research Analyst, reported that *GTA VI* (which features an 80-hour main story) has already logged nearly 16 million digital pre-orders—more than one-third of BI's first-year unit forecast—alongside near-perfect review scores on Metacritic and OpenCritic.
* **Multi-Year Revenue Model:** 
  * **Years 1 & 2:** Driven by upfront game sales at $80–$100 per copy, followed by a PC version release next year.
  * **Recurring Revenue:** The upcoming online multiplayer mode will underpin long-term recurring revenue; the previous iteration's multiplayer mode generated ~$500 million per year over 13 years.
* **Development Costs & Cloud Streaming:** Development reportedly cost upward of $1 billion (excluding marketing), though Take-Two noted it was less than the $1.5 billion cost of the Burj Khalifa. Pre-order trends have already nearly recouped this investment. Additionally, Xbox is allowing tens of millions of previous-generation Xbox One owners to play via cloud streaming.

## Lowe's Solid Quarter & Demand Uncertainty (Lindsay Dutch)
* **Q3 Performance:** Lindsay Dutch, Bloomberg Intelligence Consumer Hardlines and Beauty Retail Senior Analyst, noted Lowe's posted solid same-store sales growth of 1.8% (a 4-year best), driven by pro contractors and online sales.
* **Cautious Outlook & Weather Headwinds:** Lowe's only slightly raised its sales outlook, pointing to significant demand uncertainty for Q4 and next year. Management flagged tough weather comparisons in January; a warmer winter (such as from El Niño) without snow events would act as a headwind.
* **Housing Lock-In & Holiday Strategy:** Pending sales of existing homes hit a record low in October as homeowners cling to sub-3% mortgages, weighing on large renovation projects. However, repair and replacement demand (e.g., appliances) remains intact, and Lowe's is leaning into Black Friday/Cyber Monday promotions with curated assortments like exclusive DeWalt tools.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Nvidia's Stock & Leadership:** The probability of Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia is sub-1%, and Nvidia will be the best-performing AI stock over the next year. — *Gene Munster*
* **Target's Apparel Turnaround:** The earliest signs of Target's apparel product changes will appear in spring next year, putting the company in a better position by summer or fall next year. — *Poonam Goyal*
* ***GTA VI* Sales:** *Grand Theft Auto VI* could reach the high end of Bloomberg Intelligence's first-year sales scenario of ~16 million units. — *Nathan Naidu*
* **Take-Two's Financials:** Take-Two's free cash flow is expected to almost double this fiscal year (ending March), with double-digit growth rates continuing in FY2027 and FY2028 before normalizing in year three. — *Nathan Naidu*

## Notable Quotes
> "Nvidia is still the brains of AI, it's still the driving force behind AI and there really is no number two. And we're still early in AI." — *Gene Munster*

> "Traffic is back at Target. It was up 5%, and that is what drove the comp increase and that's extremely encouraging for Target, especially now because that was one of the biggest problems that they had to solve for." — *Poonam Goyal*

> "Based on pre-order trends, they are almost nearly there in recouping all those billion plus investments that they put into making the game." — *Nathan Naidu*

> "If there's anything negative in the print, it's really that the outlook was only slightly increased on the sales side and that really points to significant demand uncertainty for the fourth quarter and heading into next year." — *Lindsay Dutch*

briefings.title: Pirelli CEO: Formula One, Smart Tyres and Europe’s Car Industry | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: Pirelli CEO Andrea Casaluci explains how the 100-year-old company protects its margins by focusing exclusively on high-performance consumer tires—which now drive 82% of total turnover—while leveraging Formula One virtualization and the data-collecting "Cyber Tire" to prepare for autonomous driving.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Pirelli CEO Andrea Casaluci explains how the 100-year-old company protects its margins by focusing exclusively on high-performance consumer tires—which now drive 82% of total turnover—while leveraging Formula One virtualization and the data-collecting "Cyber Tire" to prepare for autonomous driving. Amidst fierce Chinese competition and European industrial policy gaps, Pirelli is investing $1 billion to scale its U.S. manufacturing capacity to 6 million tires within seven years.

## High-Value Strategy, Formula One & Virtualization
* **Pure-Play Consumer Focus:** Pirelli has exited truck, mining, and large industrial tires to focus exclusively on consumer vehicles (cars, motorcycles, and bikes) in the high-value segment.
  * **Market Dominance:** 82% of Pirelli’s total turnover—and nearly 90% in Europe—comes from high-performance tires, a segment protected from Asian budget competition by higher pricing power and OEM trust.
  * **Prestige OEMs:** Pirelli supplies top luxury automakers including Ferrari, Lamborghini, Bentley, Maserati, McLaren, Aston Martin, Porsche, and Rolls-Royce.
* **Formula One as an "Open-Air Laboratory":** Pirelli has been the sole tire supplier for Formula One since 2011, participates in 350 motorsport competitions annually, and will become the sole supplier for MotoGP starting next year.
  * **Virtualization & AI:** Because F1 teams develop tires before the actual cars exist and face strict physical testing limits, Pirelli pioneered mathematical modeling and AI simulations. Transferring this to everyday tire development has reduced time-to-market by **30%**.
  * **Brand Positioning:** F1’s 22-car grid provides global visibility every Sunday to a growing, younger, and more gender-balanced audience.
* **EV Tire Demands:** Electric vehicles require specialized tires with a higher load index (due to battery weight), stronger grip (due to instant torque), and lower noise emissions (due to the absence of engine noise).

## The Cyber Tire & Autonomous Driving
* **20 Years in the Making:** Pirelli’s "Cyber Tire" embeds sensors into the tire—the vehicle's only contact point with the road—to collect real-time data on asphalt conditions, driving style, and tire health.
  * **Current Deployment:** Already on the market with high-performance automakers including McLaren, Aston Martin, and Pagani, feeding data to systems like ABS to shorten braking distances.
* **Enabling Autonomous Vehicles:** Casaluci notes that while human drivers rely on instinct to brake or steer around obstacles, autonomous software requires a 100% data-driven "grip estimator" in real time, making the Cyber Tire critical for future self-driving cars.

## Europe’s Auto Industry, China’s Speed & US Expansion
* **Europe’s Industrial Policy Gap:** While 100% of prestige cars are still manufactured in Europe, Casaluci warns that the EU set ambitious Green Deal electrification targets without supporting them through consumer incentives or charging infrastructure.
  * **The Norway Benchmark:** Casaluci points to host Nicolai Tangen’s home country, Norway—where over 90% of new car registrations are EVs—alongside China, the Netherlands, and California as examples of effective industrial policy.
* **Learning from Chinese Speed:** Having operated in China for over 20 years, Pirelli has seen its Chinese operations evolve from a low-cost manufacturing hub into a vital R&D center serving local premium EV makers that demand low rolling resistance, high comfort, and rapid time-to-market.
  * **The Prototype Contrast:** In a recent material tender, European suppliers took two months just to return a signed NDA, whereas a Chinese supplier returned a physical prototype in the same timeframe. Casaluci attributes this to lean organizations, lack of legacy bureaucracy, and fast, single-owner decision-making.
* **The $1 Billion US Supply Chain Bet:** The U.S. represents roughly 40% of the global high-value tire market, yet Pirelli’s market share there lags behind Europe and Asia.
  * **Current Footprint:** Only 5% of Pirelli’s U.S. sales are manufactured domestically; 55% come from Mexico, and 40% are imported from Europe and South America.
  * **Resilience Over Tariffs:** Pirelli is investing $1 billion to expand its plant in Rome, Georgia, scaling production from under 500,000 tires today to 6 million tires in seven years to insulate against tariffs, currency volatility, and logistics costs.

## Leadership, Culture & Personal Philosophy
* **From Apprentice to CEO:** Casaluci joined Pirelli as an apprentice in 2002 and was appointed CEO in 2023 after 21 years, succeeding Marco Tronchetti Provera. He emphasizes knowing the vast majority of Pirelli’s 30,000 employees.
* **Collaborative Leadership:** Casaluci’s management style is built on trust, listening, and allowing teams to make—and learn from—mistakes (though not the same mistake twice).
* **Personal Balance & Routine:** He cites working too much when younger as his biggest personal mistake, advising others to stay present for family. He wakes at 7:00 AM, exercises for 50–60 minutes while listening to classical jazz (Chet Baker, Miles Davis) or classical music, and is an avid sailor who has crossed the Atlantic.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **MotoGP Sole Supplier:** Pirelli will become the sole tire supplier for MotoGP starting next year (*Andrea Casaluci*).
* **US Manufacturing Scale-Up:** Pirelli’s plant in Rome, Georgia, will scale up from under 500,000 tires to 6 million tires within 7 years (*Andrea Casaluci*).
* **Autonomous Driving Data:** Future autonomous driving decisions (braking vs. steering) will be 100% data-driven in real time, relying on grip-estimation software powered by smart tires like the Cyber Tire (*Andrea Casaluci*).

## Notable Quotes
> "Tires are the only point that touch the ground in a vehicle. And so all the vehicle performance go through tires." — **Andrea Casaluci**

> "Some European suppliers came back after two months with the NDA to be signed... The Chinese came back with a physical prototype." — **Andrea Casaluci**

> "Europe just declared the target without helping with an industrial policy... In Norway, 90% or more of the new car registrations are electric vehicles. Why? You have a fantastic industrial policy." — **Andrea Casaluci**

> "The most important ingredient we put in a tire... is the passion. The passion of people that manufacture and develop a product that will be a few weeks after in the most visible track race of the world." — **Andrea Casaluci**

briefings.title: Sam Altman on Jensen Huang, Anthropic’s IPO, And Growing AI Backlash | Future Proof
briefings.tldr: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman addressed the fallout from Jensen Huang’s ouster at Nvidia, confirmed OpenAI will eventually go public despite the downsides, and warned that "double counting" in the chip supply chain and a severe memory shortage are creating complex bottlenecks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman addressed the fallout from Jensen Huang’s ouster at Nvidia, confirmed OpenAI will eventually go public despite the downsides, and warned that "double counting" in the chip supply chain and a severe memory shortage are creating complex bottlenecks. He also attributed growing voter backlash against AI data centers to the industry's failure to assure the public that humans—not AI—will remain in control of the future.

---

## Jensen Huang, Nvidia, and Market Stability
* **Reaction to Huang’s Ouster:** Altman declined to say whether Huang should return to Nvidia, noting he doesn't know enough to answer, but called Huang a longtime hero ("Heroes have flaws") and expressed strong personal empathy given his own board ouster roughly three years ago.
* **Nvidia’s $105B Guarantee:** When host Reed Albergotti asked if Nvidia’s $105 billion guarantee for OpenAI’s Ohio data center is still solid, Altman called Nvidia a "behemoth" whose guarantees people still trust, though he acknowledged Nvidia and Huang are deeply associated.
* **Industry Resilience:** Despite the leadership upheaval, Altman argued that end-user demand and revenue growth are now strong enough that the broader AI industry will be fine.

## Public Markets & Anthropic’s IPO
* **OpenAI’s IPO Plans:** Altman confirmed OpenAI will go public at some point. While there are real downsides to being public during a volatile, high-stakes period for AI safety, he believes it is directionally good for the broader world—not just private-market investors—to have exposure.
* **Investor Demand:** Pushing back on Albergotti’s suggestion of investor skepticism around Anthropic’s upcoming IPO, Altman said skepticism comes mostly from journalists while investors remain bullish. He dismissed concerns about OpenAI going public after Anthropic, noting that over the past year there has been "way too much investor demand and not enough supply."

## Supply Chain Bottlenecks & Memory Shortages
* **"Double Counting" in Chips:** Clarifying his closed-door remarks to Samsung executives, Altman explained that historically there was one main chip provider, making demand forecasting simple. Now, multiple chipmakers are talking to the silicon supply chain assuming OpenAI, Anthropic, and others will buy *all* of their chips.
* **Shifting Constraints:** At massive scale, OpenAI’s bottlenecks have shifted unpredictably between memory, rack assembly, data center capacity, and random components like PCB laminate.
* **Consumer RAM & $7T Capex:** Addressing backlash over his comments on home computer RAM, Altman said he wants people to have plenty of RAM for home tinkering. However, he noted OpenAI warned years ago about a coming memory squeeze and the need for $7 trillion in capex. Because the industry underbuilt, DRAM prices have jumped roughly 5X to 7X.
  * **Historical reluctance:** Memory vendors have been hesitant to commit capex because the business has historically been "invest $20 billion and make $19 billion" through booms and busts, though Altman expects production to ramp up significantly now.
  * **Cloud vs. Edge:** In a supply shortage, Altman argued it is more optimal to share memory in the cloud at 100% utilization rather than having it sit idle in edge devices.

## AI Backlash, Data Centers, and Politics
* **Why Voters Hate Data Centers:** Following a Democratic "blue wave" in which all but one data center referendum bill passed, Altman blamed the backlash on a terrible industry "sales pitch"—promising cures for cancer and cheap goods in exchange for humans losing agency and "liv[ing] like a Labrador."
  * **Staying "Team Human":** Altman urged the AI industry to take a firm stance against any gradual or sudden "handover" of control to AI, ensuring humans remain in control of the future.
* **Data Center Build-Out & Debt:** Altman maintained that data centers will still get built (potentially further from communities, such as in the desert), and the ecosystem will adapt to local concerns. He dismissed fears that debt-funded build-outs are a "house of cards," pointing to unprecedented actual revenue growth and margins, while acknowledging there will be some "foam on the top."
* **Political Stance:** Altman reaffirmed his July 2025 comment that he is "politically homeless" and that Democrats have lost the culture of innovation, though he intends to work with whoever is elected. He noted he last spoke with Donald Trump at the China state dinner.

## Security, Safety, and Product Lock-In
* **Espionage & "Pragmatic Centrists":** Addressing past security incidents (including hidden cameras/microphones in conference rooms and foreign agents trying to extract pre-training secrets over drinks), Altman said OpenAI takes a "pragmatic centrist" approach to safety—neither building in total secret nor pretending AI is like any other technology.
* **Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI):** OpenAI is using its technology to build new models faster, but is *not* pushing a button for unmonitored rapid self-improvement. Altman said holding back on RSI is a deliberate tactic to keep humans in control.
* **External Evaluators:** OpenAI is working with embedded evaluators, including METR. Altman could not confirm METR's report that Anthropic doubled its capability development speed, noting progress is still too "jagged" across tasks to generalize.
* **Dots & Data Lock-In:** Responding to Albergotti’s concern that OpenAI's *Dots* product stores user memory in the cloud without export or edit controls, Altman agreed in principle that users should own and be able to export their data (as they can with ChatGPT memory). However, he noted that *Dots*' nuanced understanding of a user's life is harder to export than an iPhone camera roll (100,000 photos) or iMessage.

## The Next Wave: AI for Science
* **Beyond Chatbots and Coding:** OpenAI recently expanded free compute for academic researchers. Altman highlighted the progression from chatbots to coding agents to "AI for science"—solving historically difficult math theorems and accelerating physics, chemistry, material science, and chip design.
* **Compressing Progress:** Altman’s goal is to use AI and compute to compress 10 or 100 years of scientific discovery into a single year.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* "We will go public at some point." — Sam Altman (on OpenAI)
* "I think we will see production get ramped up a lot." — Sam Altman (on memory/chip production)
* "I think data centers will get built." — Sam Altman (on overcoming local opposition)
* "I think that the next couple of generations of models are really going to surprise people on the upside of how much they can be an engine of scientific discovery." — Sam Altman

---

## Notable Quotes
> "Jensen has long been a hero of mine. Heroes have flaws... It's hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen." — Sam Altman

> "If the sales pitch is like, we are going to offer you a cure to cancer and cheap stuff and the price of that is you are going to lose all agency and control and voice in the future, you are going to live like a Labrador... I think it's a terrible sales pitch. I don't want that world." — Sam Altman

> "I have never seen the actual revenue growth, including great margins, show up for any revolution in tech that I have witnessed in my career." — Sam Altman (on why AI data center debt is not a house of cards)

briefings.title: Satya Nadella opens Microsoft Ignite 2026
briefings.tldr: At Microsoft Ignite 2026, Satya Nadella unveiled Microsoft’s end-to-end "frontier ecosystem" built around three imperatives: keeping humans at the center, enabling organizations to own their intelligence, and establishing verifiable trust.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
At Microsoft Ignite 2026, Satya Nadella unveiled Microsoft’s end-to-end "frontier ecosystem" built around three imperatives: keeping humans at the center, enabling organizations to own their intelligence, and establishing verifiable trust. Key announcements include the broad availability of Work IQ, Copilot Workspaces, Microsoft Decision 1.1, Perception, Horizon DB (integrated into Fabric), Cobalt 200 VMs, and the Microsoft AI Transparency Initiative.

## Copilot & The Multiplayer Workplace
* **Copilot as the Work OS:** Brings together chat, co-work, code, autopilot (24/7 autonomous agents), and all of Office into one experience.
  * **Work IQ:** The underlying organizational database (people, relationships, emails, meetings, chats, projects) is now broadly available.
  * **Role-Based Extensions & Plugins:** New skills, connectors, and business plugins for sales, legal, finance, and service, including **Dynamics 365** and a new partnership with **Salesforce**.
  * **Copilot Workspaces:** A new multiplayer form factor enabling people, their agents, and other teammates to collaborate toward a shared goal with shared context.
* **GitHub Advancements:**
  * **Projects:** Allows developers to define a goal, connect repositories, and have Copilot coordinate task sessions and recurring work.
  * **GitHub Copilot Fusion:** A new composite model family that orchestrates multiple models; ranked #1 coding agent on **Terminal Bench**, scoring **5 points** over **Claude Core** at **less than half the cost**.

## Microsoft IQ, Foundry & The Model Ecosystem
* **Microsoft IQ:** Externalizes the system underneath Copilot as a first-class platform combining Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ, Web IQ, and third-party contexts, supported by **hundreds of new connectors**.
* **Microsoft Decision 1.1:** Now generally available with multimodal support, **10x faster** speed, and **200x lower cost** than using an LLM.
  * Already used by **over 4,000 customers**, including **Epic** (patient experience, clinical care, back-office) and **Xbox** (sorting tens of thousands of open-ended game launch feedback items).
* **Foundry Model Additions:** Added **GPT-62** (including **GPT-62 Astra**, which outperformed its predecessor at more than half the estimated cost), **Claude Fable 52**, **Mythos 52**, and **Meta’s** latest models.
* **MAI Model Family & Licensing:**
  * **Momentum:** **MAI Transcribe 2** requests are up **12x** since launching on OpenRouter; **MAI Code Flash** reached **3 million users** on GitHub Copilot last month; **MAI Cyber** powers **over 40%** of scans across Perception code scanning.
  * **New Models:** **Code 2** (flagship agentic coding), **Code 2 Flash** (high-volume tasks), and **Cyber 2 Flash** (integrated with Perception).
  * **MAI Licensed Weights:** Trusted partners can now access Microsoft AI model weights.
  * **Managed Agent Harness:** Foundry now offers the same harness powering Copilot, complete with continuous improvement loops and private benchmarks/evals.

## Trust, Governance & Agentic Security
* **Agent 365:** The enterprise control plane for agent governance, identity, and security already manages **50 million agents**.
  * **Agent 365 Business Analytics:** Newly announced "ERP system of AI usage" to track spend, connect it to business outcomes, and optimize ROI.
* **Perception (Generally Available):** An end-to-end agentic security system combining red team (attack simulation), blue team (detection), and green team (remediation) agents across Entra, MXC, Cloud Containers, Purview, and Defender.
  * In a recent test using the **ArtX** autonomous AI attack framework, Defender’s automated attack disruptions contained compromised accounts and isolated devices at machine speed.
* **Microsoft AI Transparency Initiative:** A three-part effort to establish open, independently verifiable industry standards for AI transparency, security, and governance—already backed by **40 organizations** and being built into MAI models, Foundry, and Copilot.

## Agent-Scale Infrastructure, Data & Silicon
* **GitHub Core Rebuild:** Decoupled storage and compute to handle agentic scale; in testing, **5,000 agents** pointed at one repo sustained **7,200 writes per second** (**180x** current throughput).
* **Azure Scale & Sustainability:** Operates **500+ data centers** across **80 Azure regions**, matching **100%** of annual global electricity consumption with renewable energy and reusing/recycling **92%** of servers and components.
* **Azure Agentic Primitives:** New micro-VMs (sub-1-second startup, full sandboxing, confidential computing enclaves), an agent grid for identity/policy-aware networking, context caching, and AKS / AKS Flex integration.
* **Horizon DB & Fabric Unification:**
  * **Horizon DB:** Distributed managed PostgreSQL database delivering **8x faster** performance than self-managed PostgreSQL, now **generally available** in Azure.
  * **Fabric Integration:** Bringing Horizon DB into Fabric unifies transactional and analytical data, allowing agents and Copilot to reason over live transactions and terabytes of historical records in real time.
* **Custom Silicon:**
  * **Cobalt 200 VMs:** Next-generation general-purpose VMs, now **generally available**.
  * **Maya 300:** Newly announced AI accelerator alongside Azure Boost and Azure Integrated HSM.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Maya 300 Efficiency:** "Maya 300... will deliver over 40% more tokens per watt compared with leading GPU systems." — Satya Nadella
* **Workplace Shift:** "Every function will go through a similar change [to software engineering] across their work, their workflow, and their work artifacts." — Satya Nadella
* **Edge AI Capabilities:** With new Windows PCs, "you can run in some sense last year's frontier models on your laptop and last quarter's models on your desktop." — Satya Nadella

## Notable Quotes
> "AI in the flow of human ambition is perhaps the biggest design challenge we have in front of us." — Satya Nadella

> "It becomes an architectural imperative to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it." — Satya Nadella

> "For an economy to remain an economy where many firms exist and thrive, intelligence by definition needs to be broadly distributed versus just collapse into a couple of models." — Satya Nadella

briefings.title: Stan Druckenmiller: Why He's "Not Playing" Right Now | TomorrowX Summit
briefings.tldr: After 50 years of investing, Stan Druckenmiller has rarely had less 12-month clarity and has shifted Duquesne Family Office into capital preservation mode ("I'm not playing"), pivoting away from his bullish January positioning as Fed tightening, widening credit spreads, and deteriorating market internals reverse the macro backdrop.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** After 50 years of investing, Stan Druckenmiller has rarely had less 12-month clarity and has shifted Duquesne Family Office into capital preservation mode ("I'm not playing"), pivoting away from his bullish January positioning as Fed tightening, widening credit spreads, and deteriorating market internals reverse the macro backdrop. Looking ahead, he is watching AI use cases—where leading labs sell tasks rather than tokens—and predicts that within 10 years we will see data centers in space, cancer become a managed disease, and a financial-crisis-driven US fiscal reform.

## Why Stan Is "Not Playing" Right Now
* **A Complete Macro Reversal:** In a conversation with Morgan Stanley's Iliana Bouzali—who runs the firm's global derivatives business and hosts macro legend Zoom calls—Druckenmiller noted he owns "almost none" of the bullish portfolio he held in January.
  * **January Backdrop:** Fed funds were at 3.5% against 6% nominal growth, the Fed dot plot signaled rate cuts, credit spreads were tight, commodities (including copper) and the advance-decline line were hitting new highs, and Claude Code had just sparked an AI capex acceleration.
  * **Today's Backdrop:** Everything has flipped. A regime change at the Fed has shifted policy from cutting to hiking after 15 years of free money and 5 years of above-target inflation. Commodities have topped (Duquesne is now short copper), credit spreads are widening, and the advance-decline line peaked on August 14th even as major averages hit highs in October.
* **Capital Preservation Mode:** Druckenmiller is neither long nor short equities—calling his equity book "basically flat" with small positions in the dollar—and refuses to short the market given ongoing AI innovation and washed-out tactical positioning.
  * **Auto-Reply:** Bouzali joked that Druckenmiller now has an auto-reply button that says, "Don't talk to me. I'm not playing."

## Risk Management, Streaks, and Investment Process
* **Four-Asset Matrix:** Duquesne trades four asset classes—commodities, bonds, stocks, and interest rates—allowing Druckenmiller to step away from equities entirely when clarity disappears, as bonds and currencies often make their biggest moves during equity bear markets.
* **P&L Over VAR:** Druckenmiller rejects Value at Risk (VAR) and stress tests because correlations break down in chaos and bear markets (as seen in software and AI infrastructure earlier in the year). Instead, **the P&L is his true signal**: if positions aren't correlating properly, he cuts back.
* **Playing Hot and Cold Streaks:** Duquesne's 50-year track record has been built in "scoops"—grinding out 5–8% years before catching a 3–4 year run, while avoiding down calendar years. Druckenmiller sizes up when he is "seeing the ball" and makes "little bunts" when he is cold.
* **Invest and Then Investigate:** Rather than waiting for complete data, Druckenmiller makes an initial bet—big enough to hurt if wrong—using about 15% of the information a traditional investor would want, based on a chart, story, or passionate pitch. He then hands it to his research team for 2–3 weeks to decide whether to add or exit.
* **What Separates Great Investors from Good Ones:**
  * **Four Core Traits:** Unbelievable passion, intellectual curiosity, competitiveness "to the point of a sickness" (no work-life balance), and strict adherence to a personal discipline.
  * **Intellectual Humility:** Smart investors often get in their own way because high IQ breeds inflexibility. Druckenmiller's twist on Mark Twain: *"Put all your eggs in one basket and then watch the basket very carefully."*
  * **Biggest Lessons:** Open-mindedness has made him the most money; breaking his own discipline out of FOMO lost him the most (selling the Nasdaq in January 2000, then buying it back within an hour of the top 26 years ago). He also noted he can tell within the first 15 minutes if someone is a phony.

## AI Use Cases: Selling Tasks, Not Tokens
* **AI Awakening:** Druckenmiller credited a guest named Gavin (introduced via Bouzali's Zoom call a month after ChatGPT launched) for waking him up to AI being "the biggest thing in the history of American business."
* **Shifting from Infrastructure to Use Cases:** While washed-out AI infrastructure stocks may offer a tactical trade, Druckenmiller does not expect them to be the multi-year engine they were over the last four years.
* **Labs Selling Tasks:** He believes leading AI labs will stop releasing models and move away from the token business. With the world's top intelligence, they can sell tasks directly and build their own businesses—particularly in **cybersecurity** (deploying swarms of agents to defend against threats they helped create) and **healthcare**.
* **AI Bear Thesis:** When asked by Bouzali which AI bear thesis he respects most, Druckenmiller pointed to **politics and financing**.

## Quiet Structural Risks Under the Surface
* **Education and Immigration:** Druckenmiller flagged the quiet deterioration of US K–12 education, which the US has historically offset by importing global talent (estimating 8 of the top 10 tech companies are run by immigrants). He worries current immigration policy threatens to cut off that talent flow.
* **The US Deficit:** Recalling his 2011–2012 college tour warning about entitlements and demographics hitting between 2020 and 2030, Druckenmiller noted the US has continued to get away with it as the reserve currency—even after $5 trillion in COVID spending and zero interest rates—but warned of a France-like fiscal reckoning.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Economic Slowdown:** The second half of 2027 could be economically disappointing, based on commodity action and defensive stocks leading cyclicals — *Stan Druckenmiller*.
* **AI Business Model Shift:** Leading AI labs will stop selling tokens and instead sell tasks directly, building their own businesses in areas like cybersecurity and healthcare — *Stan Druckenmiller*.
* **US Fiscal Crisis & Reform:** Within the next 10 years, the US will enact fiscal reform engendered by a crisis in the financial markets — *Stan Druckenmiller*.
* **Nuclear Fusion:** Within the next 10 years, there is a 20% chance we will either have fusion or it will be clear we are going to have fusion — *Stan Druckenmiller*.
* **Space Infrastructure:** Within the next 10 years, there is at least a 70% chance we will have data centers in space — *Stan Druckenmiller*.
* **Cancer:** Within 10 years (not 20), we will beat cancer and it will become a managed disease, driven by genetic sequencing, immunotherapy, and AI — *Stan Druckenmiller*.

## Notable Quotes
> "I can't remember a period where I had less clarity on where we're going to be in 12 months." — Stan Druckenmiller

> "My own belief is that they're not going to be releasing models, and if you have the number one intelligence in the world, you can start selling tasks instead of tokens." — Stan Druckenmiller

> "Put all your eggs in one basket and then watch the basket very carefully." — Stan Druckenmiller (paraphrasing Mark Twain)

> "I think we're going to beat cancer. I think it's going to be a managed disease, and I mean in 10 years, not 20 years." — Stan Druckenmiller

briefings.title: Stripe CEO Patrick Collison at Silicon Valley & The World | Semafor
briefings.tldr: Stripe CEO Patrick Collison discussed Stripe’s $7.5 billion acquisition of OpenRouter as a parallel to Stripe’s own neutral infrastructure—unifying AI tokens rather than dollars—while outlining the rise of an "AI economy" driven by agent-to-agent micropayments, the enduring value of human-made art, and the urgent need for meta-science reform.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Stripe CEO Patrick Collison discussed Stripe’s $7.5 billion acquisition of OpenRouter as a parallel to Stripe’s own neutral infrastructure—unifying AI tokens rather than dollars—while outlining the rise of an "AI economy" driven by agent-to-agent micropayments, the enduring value of human-made art, and the urgent need for meta-science reform.

## The OpenRouter Acquisition & AI Infrastructure
* **Neutral Infrastructure Parallel:** Stripe acquired OpenRouter for $7.5 billion (roughly 6x its prior valuation) after realizing both companies share the same core mission: providing neutral, unified infrastructure for everyone from solo developers to large public companies—Stripe for dollars and payment regulations, and OpenRouter for AI tokens.
* **Hyper-Growth Metrics:** 
  * Stripe grew its revenue 41% year-over-year in the first half of the year (disclosed in an investor letter).
  * OpenRouter’s volume of tokens served grew 37% month-over-month in October.
  * Collison noted that traditional valuation multiples break down at these growth rates, making it more useful to evaluate the market equilibrium 3 to 5 years out.
* **Model Diversity & Rapid Turnover:** 
  * 73% of OpenRouter’s customer usage is for models launched within the last 60 days.
  * Developers are highly sensitive to small differences across language, image, speech recognition, and decision models, driving demand for a diverse ecosystem.
* **Open-Source & Sovereignty:** Despite geopolitical concerns around Chinese open-weight models, Collison emphasized that open-source AI is essential for customers—particularly in Europe and outside the U.S.—who require sovereignty, self-hosted inference, observability, and full-stack governance.

## Agentic Commerce & The "AI Economy"
* **Machine Payments Protocol (MPP):** Stripe launched MPP a couple of months ago alongside **Tempo**, a new blockchain protocol.
  * MPP already processes tens of thousands of machine-to-machine transactions per day, though the absolute dollar volume is currently *de minimis*.
  * Many of these transactions are settled using stablecoins.
* **Pay-at-the-Moment-of-Utility:** Rather than AI agents "going on a bender," these human-driven transactions allow software to consume usage-based APIs (e.g., weather or price data) and pay instantly at the moment of utility—eliminating the need for pre-registration, advance contracts, or billing in arrears.
* **Shift to Consumption Models:** Agentic transactions are the next logical progression in a broader internet economy shift away from traditional seat-based pricing toward usage- and consumption-based models.

## Arts, Architecture, and AI Creativity
* **New Aesthetics Initiative:** Collison and economist Tyler Cowen launched *New Aesthetics*, awarding $10,000 to $250,000 grants to artists, architects, and designers.
  * Addressing moderator Reed Albergotti’s question on why Silicon Valley lags behind older industrial hubs like Detroit in funding grand cultural institutions, Collison agreed Silicon Valley should play a much bigger role in supporting the arts.
* **Breaking the "Modernist Rut":** Collison argued that architecture has been stuck in a modernist rut for a century—noting that the Bauhaus Dessau building in Germany looks like a modern Silicon Valley office—and needs a new 21st-century aesthetic.
* **Human Art in an AI Era:** Despite being deeply AI-forward, Stripe’s publishing arms (**Stripe Press** and **Works in Progress** magazine) exclusively use human-created art. Collison argued that intentionality, purpose, and relational engagement matter to consumers, and AI-generated art would make the products worse.

## Meta-Science & Research Funding
* **Arc Institute & Policy Engagement:** Collison co-founded the Arc Institute with his wife to help academic researchers avoid "grant writing hell." He recently spoke in Washington, D.C., with Michael Kratsios (head of the Office of Science and Technology Policy) about reforming basic research grants.
* **Reviving Meta-Science:** Collison noted that "meta-science"—studying how best to fund scientists (e.g., funding projects vs. funding people) and structure institutions—has been moribund for decades. He welcomed recent policy reports calling for renewed focus on these questions, especially amid the upheaval of AI.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Agent-to-Agent Transaction Volume:** Within a few years, most transactions (by volume, though not necessarily by dollar value) will be between AI agents — *Patrick Collison (referenced by Reed Albergotti and affirmed by Collison)*.
* **Emergence of Three Economies:** Going forward, the global economy will be best understood as three distinct spheres: the non-internet economy, the internet economy, and the **AI economy** — *Patrick Collison*.
* **Endurance of Open-Source AI:** The open-source AI model ecosystem "is something that's here to stay" due to international demand for inference sovereignty — *Patrick Collison*.
* **Persistence of Human Art:** Consumer and artist preference for human-created art—caring about what humans chose to depict—will persist despite the rise of AI — *Patrick Collison*.

## Notable Quotes
> "Stripe is doing this in the realm of dollars, they're doing it in the realm of tokens, that actually there were kind of deeper commonalities than might be initially apparent." — Patrick Collison

> "Going forward, I think it might be useful to think about three economies: the non-internet economy, the internet economy, and then the AI economy." — Patrick Collison

> "I've now said something controversial that'll be clipped of that modernism is a rut, but I'll stand by it." — Patrick Collison

> "All of the art for Stripe Press and for Works in Progress is created by humans... I think people care about that fact and they want to know what humans chose to depict. It would be less interesting if it was AI art." — Patrick Collison

briefings.title: The Boomerang CEO(s): With MongoDB’s Dev Ittycheria
briefings.tldr: MongoDB CEO Dev Ittycheria—who returned after a 10-month retirement following an 11-year run—breaks down the core job of a CEO into three non-negotiable pillars: setting strategy, putting the right people on the bus, and creating an environment where they can win.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
MongoDB CEO Dev Ittycheria—who returned after a 10-month retirement following an 11-year run—breaks down the core job of a CEO into three non-negotiable pillars: setting strategy, putting the right people on the bus, and creating an environment where they can win. In an era of AI-driven speed, he argues that a CEO’s toughest calls test courage rather than intelligence, requiring radical candor, fast decision-making, and a relentless hunt for bad news.

## The Three Jobs of a CEO & The Boomerang Return
* **The Core Framework:** Credited to former Palo Alto Networks CEO Mark McLaughlin, Dev Ittycheria defines the CEO role by three responsibilities; doing 997 other things well while failing at these three means failing as a CEO:
  * **Strategy:** Defining where the company is going and what it aspires to be (which changes infrequently).
  * **People:** Ensuring the right core leadership team is on the bus to execute the strategy (which requires constant assessment).
  * **Environment:** Making capital allocation decisions and building a culture ("culture as a product") that attracts, retains, and sets people up for success.
* **The Return to MongoDB:** After retiring for 10 months to spend time with family and join Sequoia, Dev received a call in Tuscany from the board chair that his successor was resigning. He returned within a week out of responsibility to MongoDB's 6,000 employees, thousands of customers, and investor base—just ahead of an Investor Day and their largest user conference in New York.
* **Immediate Restructuring:** Upon returning, Dev simplified the organization by consolidating product—which his predecessor had split into two groups—and bringing in an interim executive to cover a vacant role, aiming to eliminate ambiguity and accelerate decision-making.

## Speed, Truth, and Confrontation
* **Decision Velocity:** A company is the sum of its decisions; the best companies make good decisions quickly over a long period.
* **The Vulnerability Secret:** Dev admits his intensity can intimidate people, so he uses vulnerability—admitting his own mistakes and knowledge gaps—to create psychological safety. When leaders admit mistakes, teams mimic them, surface truth faster, and solve problems more quickly.
* **Confrontation Over Conflict Aversion:** Avoiding issues causes them to fester; if a team knows an issue exists and the CEO ignores it, the CEO becomes the problem by lowering the standard.
* **The Asymmetry of Information:** Outside the company (Glassdoor, Blind, X, Wall Street), bad news is overrepresented. Inside the company, good news finds the CEO automatically, while bad news travels slowly upward and is often sanitized. Dev assumes any bad news he hears is both late and worse than reported, so he actively hunts for it.

## Scaling Leadership & Evaluating Talent
* **Courage Over Intelligence:** Over 11 years at MongoDB, Dev went through 23 C-level executives. The hardest calls were not intellectual, but emotional—deciding to put the company ahead of loyal early executives who could not scale to the next stage.
  * **Tells of an Unscalable Exec:** Lack of self-awareness, losing their team ("you can fool people above you, sometimes around you, never below you"), and declining hiring quality.
* **What Dev Looks for in a Successor CEO:**
  * **Ownership Mindset:** Treating the business as if it is 100% of their net worth, owned for 100 years (citing Warren Buffett).
  * **Long-Term Orientation:** Avoiding myopic, transactional decisions driven by 6-to-12-month stock price targets or short-term equity triggers.
  * **People Development:** Going beyond recruiting and execution to actively coaching, giving constructive feedback, and holding people accountable.
  * **Crisis & AI Thinking:** Distinguishing "builders" from "harvesters" during downturns, and having a clear point of view on how AI impacts org design, capital allocation, and innovation.
* **Evaluating Founders & CROs:**
  * **Founders:** Brian Halligan (HubSpot CEO & Sequoia partner) and Dev debate raw compute (e.g., math Olympiad/chess prodigies) versus wisdom, taste, and judgment. Dev argues that in a world where intelligence is ubiquitous and cheap, intellectual humility, taste, and the ability to learn ("student of the game") matter more than being the "smartest kid in the class."
  * **CROs:** Dev warns against "cut-and-paste" playbooks, noting that infrastructure sales (like MongoDB's) require winning over developers, security, ops, and economic buyers, unlike many application sales. He looks for CROs who succeeded selling a second- or third-tier product against a strong incumbent rather than riding inbound demand at a market leader, and stresses conducting blind reference checks.

## Operating in the AI Era
* **What Has Changed for Modern CEOs:**
  * **Shorter Decision Half-Lives:** The world moves too fast to punt on decisions; most decisions today are two-way doors, making speed a primary weapon.
  * **Token & Unit Economics:** With compute and GPU costs, CEOs must understand gross margins and the value delivered on top of consumed tokens.
  * **Talent Density:** Companies can do much more with fewer people, placing an even higher premium on top talent.
  * **Modulating Euphoria and Panic:** Founders must keep egos in check during inbound surges (warning against COVID-style overhiring and bloat) and keep teams steady when new models drop.
* **Planning & Focus:** While running 12-month planning cycles, Dev recasts plans every 90 days to align expenses with real revenue and ruthlessly cut underperforming projects.
* **Brian Halligan’s Takeaways for HubSpot:** Returning as CEO of HubSpot, Brian is applying Dev’s advice by encouraging employees to act as if they own 100% of HubSpot shares, making faster two-way-door decisions, obsessing over leading indicators (usage, NPS, unit economics), and maintaining a steady presence between high highs and low lows.

## Notable Quotes
> "I can do a thousand things. I can do this podcast, I can go visit customers, but if I do 997 things well and these three things [strategy, people, environment] poorly, I fail as a CEO." — Dev Ittycheria

> "I think the toughest decisions I faced were not the ones that tested my intelligence, they tested my courage." — Dev Ittycheria

> "If you're not embarrassed by who you were two, three years ago, you're not growing fast enough." — Dev Ittycheria

> "Most things are two-way doors today. You can build so fast, you can change your mind on most things. So I think speed is a weapon these days." — Brian Halligan

briefings.title: Washington Today (11-17-26): Transp. Sec. Duffy meets Senate GOP on $50B request for ATC upgrades
briefings.tldr: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy briefed Senate Republicans on the Trump administration's updated $50.1 billion emergency request to modernize FAA air traffic control systems following a nationwide ground stop of over 9,000 flights, amid a broader wave of tech outages at the NSA, major banks, and Apple.
